inputs.fcf_basis_note: FY2025 FCF of $26,914M used as base. H1 FY2026 FCF is already $18,272M (annualized ~$36.5B), confirming the high Y1 growth rate assumption is conservative. FCF is the appropriate primary driver given: (1) GAAP EPS is depressed by VMware acquisition amortization ($9-10B/yr in intangibles) and integration charges; (2) Shareholders equity is artificially inflated by ~$54B of VMware goodwill/intangibles, making equity CAGRs unreliable as a business performance measure. FCF is the cleanest metric per Broadcom management's own guidance framework and FCF margin (~42%) is the highest-quality indicator of value creation.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (3yr: 53.0%, 5yr: 27.8%) is distorted by the November 2023 VMware acquisition which added ~$54B in goodwill and intangibles to the balance sheet, inflating shareholders equity from ~$24B (FY2023) to ~$68B (FY2024) and ~$81B (FY2025). This is an accounting artifact, not organic value creation. Equity CAGR diverges >30pp from FCF and Revenue CAGRs on the 3-year basis, meeting the flag threshold. Additionally, GAAP EPS is depressed by ~$9-10B/yr in non-cash VMware amortization charges, making EPS CAGRs also unreliable. FCF CAGR is the most reliable and consistent metric, used as the selected rate. The actual growth trajectory is accelerating well above the 5yr FCF CAGR: FY2026 FCF is on track for ~$36-40B (per H1 FY2026 actuals of $18.3B and Q3 guidance), implying ~35-50% YoY FCF growth, driven by the AI semiconductor ramp. The DCF scenarios therefore start with elevated Year 1 growth rates (25-50%) decelerating toward terminal, rather than anchoring mechanically on historical CAGR. This is appropriate: Broadcom is NOT a mid-cycle cyclical but a secular growth compounder in the early stages of an AI infrastructure buildout. Mid-cycle normalization would severely understate intrinsic value.
historical_growth.eps_5yr_cagr_note: EPS 5yr CAGR of 49.9% is artificially high because FY2020 EPS ($0.63) was depressed by COVID and because FY2025 EPS ($4.77) still reflects partial VMware amortization headwinds. Not used as primary driver.

assumptions.wacc_rationale: WACC of 10% (base) reflects: large-cap, investment-grade technology company (Moody's A3, S&P A-); elevated but declining leverage (~2.4x Net Debt/EBITDA post-VMware); AI-cycle and customer concentration risk premiums; and current interest rate environment. Bull case uses 9% (credit rating improvement as debt is paid down, lower risk premium as AI revenue diversifies across 6+ hyperscalers). Bear case uses 11% (concentration risk materializes, debt concerns resurface, macro tightening).
assumptions.terminal_growth_rationale: Terminal growth of 3.0% (base) reflects long-run nominal GDP growth. Broadcom's software segment provides recurring subscription revenue that could sustain above-GDP terminal growth, while semiconductor markets are more cyclical. Bull 3.5% accounts for continued AI infrastructure secular growth; Bear 2.5% assumes commoditization pressure.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (40%): H1 FY2026 FCF already $18.3B annualized to ~$36.5B, implying ~36% YoY. AI semiconductor revenue guided to $56B in FY2026 (+180% YoY), driving significant margin expansion. Year 2 (30%): AI ramp continues toward management's $100B+ FY2027 target. Year 3-5: Deceleration as AI ramp matures, VMware monetization plateaus, and hyperscaler capex growth moderates. Terminal 10% represents normalization toward infrastructure-like growth.

bull.growth_rationale: AI ramp exceeds $56B FY2026 guidance; management's $100B+ FY2027 target for AI semiconductor revenue alone achieved; VMware monetization accelerates with VCF 9.1 AI capabilities; Apple AI infrastructure wins materialize. FCF margins expand above 45% as software mix increases.

bear.growth_rationale: AI capex digestion causes hyperscaler spending pause in late 2026/2027; Google or Meta delays next XPU generation; Apple wireless revenue declines faster; VMware churn from pricing aggression exceeds expectations; China export restrictions reduce Asia-Pacific revenue. FCF growth decelerates sharply.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC (8% to 12%), Columns = Terminal Growth Rate (2.0% to 4.0%). Values are intrinsic value per share in USD.

sanity_check.historical_broadcom_pe_range: 20x-40x non-GAAP earnings (GAAP distorted by amortization; non-GAAP P/E typically 25-35x). Stock has re-rated to 35-45x non-GAAP since AI growth emerged in 2023.
sanity_check.historical_broadcom_ev_ebitda_range: 18x-30x adjusted EBITDA over 5-year period, with recent expansion to 35-50x on AI growth premium.
sanity_check.assessment: The base case DCF intrinsic value of $172.47/share implies 36.2x FY2025 GAAP P/E and 20.8x EV/EBITDA — both WITHIN Broadcom's historical trading range. This is NOT a failure of the model; rather, it tells us that the current market price of $380.15 (79.7x GAAP P/E, 44.5x EV/EBITDA) prices in growth assumptions SUBSTANTIALLY more aggressive than the base case. The current stock price is pricing in near-perfect execution: AI revenue toward $100B+ management guidance by FY2027, sustained margin expansion, and a terminal multiple well above historical norms. The bull case IV of $299.36 implies 62.8x GAAP P/E and 34.2x EV/EBITDA — approaching the top of Broadcom's historical range and still -21.3% below current price. This is a high-conviction growth company trading at a significant premium to DCF-derived intrinsic value across all three scenarios. Broadcom is a legitimate growth compounder with exceptional FCF generation, but the current valuation requires continued AI infrastructure spending at unprecedented scale, flawless hyperscaler execution, and VMware monetization success — all simultaneously. The 79.7x GAAP P/E is not unprecedented for AI-growth leaders but does leave minimal margin of safety.
sanity_check.fix_rationale: No adjustment made. The model correctly reflects that AVGO is significantly overvalued relative to DCF-derived intrinsic value under reasonable assumptions. The premium is explained by AI growth optionality and market momentum, not a modeling error. A value investor's appropriate response is to recognize the current price as growth-case pricing and either wait for a pullback or demand a bull-case-plus scenario to justify the current price.
sanity_check.what_would_justify_current_price: To justify $380.15 under a 10% WACC and 3% terminal growth, Broadcom would need to sustain: Year 1-3 FCF growth of ~70-80% (vs our base case 40/30/20%), implying FY2026 FCF of ~$45B+ (vs ~$37-40B annualized run-rate). This requires the $56B AI semiconductor revenue guidance to flow through to FCF at high margins AND VMware software to continue growing. Under a 9% WACC (3.5% terminal growth), it would require ~55-60% Y1 growth and higher Y2-5 rates — within the bounds of the bull case trajectory if AI revenue tracks toward $100B+ in FY2027.
